learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will master the use of present, past, and future tenses, focusing on complex forms like perfect and perfect continuous to sequence events accurately.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Think of verbs as time travelers. Tenses are the dials on their time machine, telling us exactly *when* the action takes place—yesterday, right now, or in the distant future! ⏳

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Present tenses ground us in current habits, universal truths, or ongoing actions. Simple Present is for facts/habits. Present Continuous is for actions happening right now. Present Perfect connects the past to the present, and Present Perfect Continuous shows an action that started in the past and is still ongoing.
examples_or_templates: Simple: The Earth revolves around the sun. (Fact)
Perfect: I have lived here for five years. (Past action connecting to present)

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Past tenses describe completed actions. Simple Past is for finished events. Past Continuous sets the scene with ongoing past actions. Past Perfect is the 'past of the past' (used when one action finishes before another).
examples_or_templates: Continuous: I was reading when the lights went out. (Interrupted action)
Perfect: The train had left before we reached the station. (First action completed)

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Future tenses predict or plan. Simple Future (will/shall) is for sudden decisions or facts. Future Continuous is for actions that will be ongoing. Future Perfect implies an action will be completed by a specific time in the future.
examples_or_templates: Simple: I will help you with your homework. (Sudden decision)
Perfect: By next year, she will have graduated. (Action finished by a deadline)

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which tense correctly completes the sentence? 'I _____ for two hours when my friend finally arrived.'
❓ Identify the correct form: 'The sun _____ in the east.'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Complete the sentence with the correct tense: 'By the time you wake up tomorrow, I _____ (leave) for the airport.'
subjective_practice.hint: You need a tense that shows an action will be completed before a certain time in the future.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Correct the error: 'I am knowing him since 2015.'
subjective_practice.hint: Stative verbs like 'know' are rarely used in the continuous (-ing) form. What is the correct perfect tense to use with 'since'?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank: 'While I _____ (study), my brother was playing video games.'
subjective_practice.hint: Two ongoing actions were happening at the same time in the past.

activity_or_assignment.title: 📰 The Time Travel Journalist
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Write a 3-paragraph diary entry. Paragraph 1: Describe what you did yesterday (Past Tenses). Paragraph 2: Describe what you are doing right now and your current habits (Present Tenses). Paragraph 3: Describe your goals for next year (Future Tenses).

chapter_summary: ⭐ Present, Past, and Future tenses have four sub-categories: Simple, Continuous, Perfect, and Perfect Continuous.
⭐ Past Perfect requires two past actions, highlighting which one happened first.
⭐ Use 'since' for a specific point in time and 'for' for a duration of time.
